next.name: Threat Group-3390
next.headline: Threat Group-3390 (Emissary Panda, APT27): a long-running espionage group that vendors say targets industry and…
next.in_short: Vendors track Threat Group-3390 under many names. Reports describe watering-hole attacks, exploited servers and the HyperBro backdoor, aimed at industry, government and telecoms. Attribution to a country comes from named sources.

sentences.t: Threat Group-3390 is tracked under many names, including Emissary Panda, APT27, LuckyMouse, Iron Tiger, BRONZE UNION and Linen Typhoon.
Dell SecureWorks researchers designated the group Threat Group 3390 and nicknamed it Emissary Panda in 2015. The article describes it as believed to be based in China.
Symantec lists LuckyMouse, Emissary Panda and APT27 as other names for the group it calls Budworm. It believes Budworm has been active since at least 2013.
Germany's domestic intelligence agency, the BfV, describes APT27 as a Chinese cyberespionage group.
SecureWorks said most early targets were in the automotive, electronic, aerospace, energy and pharmaceutical industries. At least 50 organizations in the US and the United Kingdom had data stolen.
The same research also named defense contractors, universities, law firms and political organizations as targets.
Symantec says Budworm often focuses on government, technology and defense organizations. In August 2023 it hit a Middle Eastern telecommunications organization and an Asian government.
The BfV says APT27 has repeatedly attacked German companies since at least March 2021.
A Malpedia entry says the HyperBro backdoor has been seen mainly against the gambling industry, though it has appeared elsewhere too.

In 2015, SecureWorks reported that the group broke into networks largely through watering-hole attacks launched from over 100 compromised websites. It used no zero-days, relying on old flaws such as CVE-2011-3544 and CVE-2010-0738, and used the PlugX remote access tool.
The same report says the group appears to have used China's Baidu search engine to research targets.
The BfV says APT27 got in through unpatched, internet-exposed servers, using flaws in Microsoft Exchange and Zoho ManageEngine ADSelfService Plus. The final payload was HyperBro.
The Malpedia entry says HyperBro typically has three or more parts. These include a genuine loader and an encrypted, compressed payload with its command-server details built in.
Symantec says Budworm loads its SysUpdate backdoor by DLL sideloading. It also uses built-in and publicly available tools to map networks and dump credentials.

Symantec reports that in August 2023 Budworm used an updated SysUpdate variant against the two victims above. Only credential harvesting was seen, so Symantec says the activity may have been stopped early.
Symantec says the targets suggest intelligence gathering as the motive.
In a July 2025 report, Microsoft said it observed Linen Typhoon, one of two named Chinese nation-state actors, exploiting flaws in on-premises SharePoint servers.
An eSentire report on a ransomware intrusion says its tactics resemble those of Emissary Panda. It stresses it has no strong evidence linking the two, and says the overlap could be a false flag.
Patch internet-facing servers promptly and watch for unfamiliar web shells and DLL sideloading.
